**Chameleon templates, modernized. Several times faster.**

chameleon-rs is [Chameleon](https://github.com/malthe/chameleon)'s template language on a new
engine written in Rust. Your existing templates and code run unchanged, with byte-identical
output, several times faster. It also adds what a modern Python web app expects: async
rendering that never blocks the event loop, built-in integrations for Flask/Quart, FastAPI,
Starlette, Robyn and Litestar, partials, Markdown, and support for free-threaded Python. No
runtime dependencies.

**Source on GitHub: <https://github.com/mikeckennedy/chameleon-rs>** ·
[Changelog](https://github.com/mikeckennedy/chameleon-rs/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) ·
[Issues](https://github.com/mikeckennedy/chameleon-rs/issues)

```python
from chameleon_rs import PageTemplate

page = PageTemplate('<p tal:repeat="name names">Hello, ${name}!</p>')
print(page(names=['World', 'Rust']))
```

```html
<p>Hello, World!</p>
<p>Hello, Rust!</p>
```

## Install

```bash
uv pip install chameleon-rs
```

CPython 3.12 to 3.15, including the free-threaded builds (3.14t, 3.15t). The wheels for Linux,
macOS and Windows include the compiled engine, so you don't need a Rust toolchain, and stock
Chameleon doesn't need to be installed.

## Already on Chameleon?

Put this at the very top of your app's entry point, before anything imports Chameleon:

```python
import chameleon_rs.compat

chameleon_rs.compat.install()
```

From then on `import chameleon` gives chameleon-rs, and so do `chameleon_partials`,
`chameleon_flask`, `fastapi_chameleon` and `chameleon_robyn`. Templates and code stay as they
are.

- **Same output.** Chameleon's own test suite passes unmodified, all 122 of its fixture
  templates render byte-identical, and so does every page of two production Flask/Quart sites.
  See [Compatibility](user-guide/compatibility.qmd).
- **Check your own app first.** Shadow mode renders a sample of real traffic with both engines
  and reports any difference, while Chameleon keeps serving. See
  [Switching from Chameleon](user-guide/switching-from-chameleon.qmd).

## Starting fresh?

Chameleon templates are HTML with `tal:` attributes and `${...}` expressions, so a template is
still valid HTML that an editor or browser opens as-is. Point chameleon-rs at a folder and
decorate your views. With FastAPI:

```python
import fastapi

import chameleon_rs.fastapi as chameleon

app = fastapi.FastAPI()
chameleon.configure(template_folder='templates', app=app)


@app.get('/episodes/{number}')              # the route decorator first...
@chameleon.template('episodes/detail.pt')   # ...then @template
async def detail(number: int):
    episode = await db.episode(number)
    if episode is None:
        chameleon.not_found()
    return {'episode': episode}
```

[Getting started](user-guide/getting-started.qmd) walks through it, and
[Web frameworks](user-guide/frameworks.qmd) shows the same page in every framework.

## What's new compared with Chameleon

- **[Errors where the mistake is](user-guide/strict-tags.qmd).** An unclosed tag carrying
  `tal:` attributes makes Chameleon render what a condition should hide, or fail lines away
  with an unrelated `NameError`. With `strict_tags=True` it's a `ParseError` pointing at that
  tag and naming the missing end tag. Opt-in.
- **[Async rendering](user-guide/async.qmd).** `await template.render_async(**model)` awaits
  awaitable model values where the template uses them, without blocking the event loop. Opt-in
  settings run helpers and partials concurrently.
- **[Web frameworks](user-guide/frameworks.qmd).** Flask and Quart, FastAPI, Starlette (a
  drop-in for `Jinja2Templates`), Robyn and Litestar (a template engine for `TemplateConfig`)
  are built in; Pyramid's pyramid_chameleon and Zope/Plone's z3c.pt run unchanged.
- **[Partials](user-guide/partials.qmd).** `${render_partial('shared/card.pt', item=item)}`
  works in every template and renders natively, about 10x faster than Chameleon with
  chameleon_partials.
- **[HTMX](user-guide/htmx.qmd).** Built-in partials are HTMX fragments: the page includes
  one with `render_partial`, and the HTMX view returns the same template on its own.
- **[Markdown](user-guide/markdown.qmd).** `${markdown: post.body}` converts CommonMark plus
  the GitHub extensions while the page renders, in Rust, with raw HTML escaped by default:
  about 26x faster than mistune, a pure-Python converter.
- **[One place for settings](user-guide/configuration.qmd).** `chameleon_rs.configure()` sets
  the template folder, reloading, partial lookup and Markdown for the whole process.
- **Free-threaded Python.** Wheels for 3.14t and 3.15t that keep the GIL off.
- **[Long-standing Chameleon issues fixed](user-guide/compatibility.qmd#chameleon-bugs-fixed).**
  `pathlib.Path` works wherever a path string does, Zope's `repeat.item.first('category')` and
  `last('category')` group a sorted sequence, valueless attributes given a value render
  `disabled="disabled"`, `repeat.item` stays right in a recursive macro, a macro call no longer
  resets a local that shadows a global, and errors inside `metal:fill-slot` point at the fill's
  failing expression.
- **Typed.** Type information for the whole API, checked with `ty`.

## Fast

Rendering is about 4x to 7x faster than Chameleon on synthetic pages, and 2.2x faster across
the pages of a production site, where the app's own Python code takes much of the time.
Templates compile about 70x faster, so the first request after a deploy or reload is quick
too. See [Performance](user-guide/performance.qmd).

![](https://mkennedy-shared.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/github/chamelon-rs-perf-graph-performance.svg){fig-alt="chameleon-rs speedup over Chameleon: native partials 10.9x, macro calls 6.9x, listings 6.6x, app-shaped page 4.3x, template compilation about 70x; on a production Quart site, template rendering 2.2x, throughput 1.34x, whole requests 1.3x"}
